correctness.rationale: Decompose the five-cube using the mean and the 4-dimensional centered contrast space with Jacobian sqrt(5). The CDF is the integral of (1-range)_+. The unrestricted term equals the classical exact n=5 low-tail polynomial. For r^2<=2/3 two distinct positive violations v_i-v_j>1 cannot occur: their ordered-pair Gram inner products are at most 1, giving least simultaneous squared radius 2/(2+q)>=2/3, with reverse inequalities infeasible. Thus the positive correction sums 20 identical integrals over 3-ball cross-sections, evaluated explicitly. Beta expansion of the positive integral gives the exact 7/2 threshold exponent and coefficient. A 406-check verifier independently reconstructs the low-tail coefficient using Gaussian order statistics and checks Gram pair cases, quadratures, endpoint numbers and derivative identities. Infinite-domain validity is proved by the geometric argument, not finite checks.

value.rationale: The finite-sample variance distribution under a bounded uniform parent is an explicitly motivated statistic for acceptance limits. This yields a natural complete consecutive CDF branch at the first dimension not addressed by the recent n=4 elementary closure theorem and passes the first new clipping transition, rather than tabulating an arbitrary point or adding a routine constant. The exact noninteger 7/2 onset quantifies smoothness loss, and the 1/6 endpoint marks the first true overlap and the limit of this capwise method. No full-support n=5 theorem or downstream general result is claimed.
